title: Algebraicity of a classifying stack forces flat finite-presentation groups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $G$ be a group algebraic space over $B$: an algebraic space $G$ with a morphism $G\to B$, multiplication $G\times_B G\to G$, identity $B\to G$ and inverse $G\to G$ satisfying the group laws on every test scheme. Form the groupoid in algebraic spaces with objects $B$, arrows $G$, both source and target equal to $G\to B$, and composition equal to multiplication. Let $[B/G]$ denote the stackification of this groupoid on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], using the fibred-groupoid conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. If $[B/G]$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], then $G\to B$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, with these properties tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No flatness, local finite type, smoothness, separation or quasi-compactness is assumed on $G\to B$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-quotient-flat-refinement] to the groupoid $(B,G)$ in the statement. Obtain $g:B'\to B$ such that $h:B'\times_B G\to B$ is sheaf-surjective and the two projections of $R'=B'\times_B G\times_B B'$ to $B'$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. Indeed both arrow endpoints are the structure map $G\to B$, so the displayed fibre products are exactly the restricted arrows and the morphism $h$ of that criterion; no action-groupoid comparison is needed.

source.place: Tag 06PL (lemma-BG-algebraic), converse: apply the general quotient criterion 06PJ (which also supplies the special case 06PK cited by the source).

proof.text: The sheaf fibre products below are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The morphism $g$ is itself sheaf-surjective: given $b\in B(T)$, a local lift $(b',a)$ through $h$ has $g(b')=b$. Put $Y=G\times_B B'$ and let $u:R'\to Y$ forget the first $B'$ coordinate. This is sheaf-surjective as well: for $(a,b'_2)\in Y(T)$, locally lift its common image in $B(T)$ through $g$ to $b'_1$ and use $(b'_1,a,b'_2)$. The composite $R'\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}B'$, with $v(a,b'_2)=b'_2$, is the last projection of Step 1.

source.place: Tag 06PL (lemma-BG-algebraic), converse: sheaf surjectivity of B-prime to B and of its indicated base change, with local lifts written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-sheaf-surjective-property-descent] to $R'\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}B'$, once for flatness and once for local finite presentation. Step 1 gives each property for $vu$ and Step 2 gives sheaf-surjectivity of $u$. Thus $v:G\times_B B'\to B'$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. In particular this deduction has not assumed that $g$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 06PL (lemma-BG-algebraic), converse: the application of spaces-descent Tag 06NR.

proof.text: We use [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] for maps of algebraic spaces. They are discrete algebraic stacks: their sheaf condition gives effective descent with identity isomorphisms, their diagonal is representable, and their etale scheme atlas is smooth [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. The last cited node also makes every map of spaces representable by algebraic spaces. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $T\to B$. Sheaf-surjectivity of $g$ gives an fppf scheme covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ with maps $T_i\to B'$ over $B$. Form $W=\coprod_iT_i$ and its glued map to $B'$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The maps $T_i\to T$ are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-pc-fppf-site]. The calculus node checks these properties on the disjoint open cover of $W$, so $W\to T$ has both; it is surjective because the covering is jointly surjective. The calculus node also base changes Step 3 along $W\to B'$, giving flatness and local finite presentation of $G\times_B W\to W$. Its identification with $(G\times_B B')\times_{B'}W$ sends $((a,b'),w)$ to $(a,w)$, with inverse $(a,w)\mapsto((a,b'(w)),w)$. All covering indices and coproducts are taken in the fixed universe.

source.place: Tag 06PL (lemma-BG-algebraic), converse: choose the local lifts of B-prime over an etale scheme atlas and assemble the fppf cover; base change of the properties obtained by 06NR.

proof.text: Apply the algebraic-space clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] to $G\times_B T\to T$ and the surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme map $W\to T$ of Step 4. Its base change is $G\times_B W\to W$: a test-section triple $((a,t),w)$ with $t$ the image of $w$ is precisely $(a,w)$. Hence $G\times_B T\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, separately. Finally choose any surjective etale scheme chart $U\to G\times_B T$. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] with target $T$ first gives both properties for $U\to T$, and with target chart $T\to B$ gives both for $G\to B$. No quasi-compactness of either cover was needed. If $B$ is empty, all spaces over it are empty and the same chart tests are vacuous.

lean.statement: theorem algebraic_classifying_stack_flatness {S : Scheme.{u}} {B G : AlgebraicSpace S} (p : G ⟶ B) (e : B.obj.obj ⟶ G.obj.obj) (i : G.obj.obj ⟶ G.obj.obj) (m : Limits.pullback p.hom.hom p.hom.hom ⟶ G.obj.obj) (F : BasedCategory.{max u v, max (u + 1) w} (Over S)) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli B.obj.obj) F) (presentation : SpaceGroupoidQuotientPresentation p.hom.hom p.hom.hom e i m F a) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) : MapIsFlat p ∧ MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation p
lean.note: The group operations and the fppf stackification are specified by the algebraic-space quotient presentation with identical endpoints. The conclusion uses the shared etale chart predicates; no finiteness, separation or flatness hypothesis is added.
